newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: US-Israeli JV wins six power plants in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: US-Israeli JV wins six power plants in Kazakhstan.

text.p: AES Suntree Power, a joint venture of U.S. independent power producer AES Corp and Israel's Suntree Power, said on Tuesday it was buying four power plants and would manage another two in east Kazakhstan.
"We are pleased to take over and purchase a large part of the energy capacity of eastern Kazakhstan," AES President Dennis Bakke told a news conference.

He said the contract finally agreed with the former Soviet republic's government provides for the concession on two hydro- electric power stations and the purchase of four combined heat and power stations.
The contract followed AES Suntree Power's victory earlier this month in an international tender announced in March.
The total electric capacity of the stations in the transaction is 1,400 megawatts, with additional thermal capacity of over 1,000 megawatts electric equivalent.

Under the contract, AES Suntree Power will pay the Kazakh government a bonus of $20.7 million for the concession on the two hydro stations, which will last for 20 years and may be extended for another five years.
Up to $4.5 million will be paid for 100 percent shares in the four thermal powers stations.
"An investment programme of approximately $600 million will be implemented," said the press release of AES Suntree Power.

Sarybay Kalmyrzayev, in charge of the finance ministry's state property department, told Reuters the U.S.-Israeli venture would also pay off a total of $56 million of the power plants' debts to other companies and wage arrears to their workers.

Commenting on the low price offered for the stations, Kalmyrzayev said: "The price is not bad, taking into account that the "youngest" of the stations was built in 1961 and all of them are in a poor technical condition."
AES already owns a thermal power power plant in Ekibastuz in northern Kazakhstan, with a capacity of 4,000 megawatts.
"The hydro stations have a low cost basis and combined with our Ekibastuz power station give us some of the lowest cost power in all of Kazakhstan," the press release said.

Bakke said that the companies run by his company in Kazakhstan -- a vast Central Asian state five times the size of France and populated by just 16.7 million people -- could eventually start exporting cheap electricity to nearby China.
"Our company is already the largest non-Chinese electricity producer in China," he said.
Bakke said that the deal with the Kazakh government brings the number of power plants operated by AES worldwide to around 90 with a total power capacity of over 25,000 megawatts.

The sale of the six stations was part of Kazakhstan's privatisation programme, in which most of the energy-rich Central Asian state's oil, gas and electricity infrastructure are being sold to foreign investors.

The government has already attracted to the economy over $3.5 billion of direct foreign investment, including over $2 billion in the energy sector. Investment commitments are estimated at up to $50 billion.
